historical_reviews.deepseek: The GET can capture baseline/after metadata but omits every mutating and cryptographic checkpoint and uses unsafe authentication/TLS patterns.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly retains CSR-sign-upload-verify intent while refusing literal default credentials, `-k`, token exposure and unapproved Apache/key handling.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The Apache block is executable only if the owner designates an isolated PKI workstation and maps its artifacts into an authorized CA chain. The literal `server.crt/key` versus `Server_CA.crt/key` placeholders cannot be guessed or treated as production trust material.

original_test_intent: Generate and sign a BMC HTTPS CSR, replace the active BMC HTTPS certificate, and prove the installed certificate information and TLS service are correct.
original_method: Snapshot the exact BMC certificate and recovery state; use an owner-approved PKI workstation/CA and profile to generate the BMC CSR, validate it, issue the server certificate and chain, preflight the CertificateService target and rollback artifact, perform one approved replacement through protected authentication, validate the new TLS identity/service from a separate client, and restore the original certificate if required.
manual_activity: A certificate owner approves the CA, profile, Apache/workstation scope, target certificate slot and final/rollback state; an operator verifies the physical target, authorizes replacement, observes console recovery and owns the verdict.
required_inputs: Key algorithm, length, usage and validity policy
Mapped PKI workstation/Apache role and artifact paths
Active certificate export or supported rollback artifact
Post-install trust client and acceptance criteria
safety_requirements: Never use literal default credentials, sample token or `-k`
Do not expose CA keys, BMC private keys, passwords, cookies or tokens
Do not install/enable Apache on an unspecified host
Verify CSR public key, SAN, chain, validity and key usage before replacement
Confirm exact target certificate slot and same BMC before POST
Perform one replacement only; never retry blindly
Stop on TLS loss, wrong certificate, key exposure or schema mismatch
Keep console recovery and rollback artifact ready
agent_execution_scope: Capture redacted active certificate and TLS baseline
Generate/parse the approved CSR without exporting its private key
Validate issued public certificate and chain
Submit one approved protected certificate replacement
Verify installed metadata, trust and BMC Web/Redfish reachability
Restore baseline when directed and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve CA/profile, host roles and artifact mapping
Approve certificate URI and final-versus-restored state
Provide protected signing and authentication mechanisms
Authorize the replacement and watch recovery
Resolve TLS failure and assign PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A certificate inventory read is baseline evidence only and cannot generate/sign a CSR, replace the HTTPS certificate or prove client trust afterward.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use approved PKI tooling and the documented BMC CertificateService action with protected session authentication, after chain/SAN/slot preflight and with one-shot rollback readiness; validate from an independent trust client.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The specified Taiwan/Taipei/Wistron/PV identity, RSA-2048 request, 365-day example, CSR inspection, replacement and 30/10-minute estimates are preserved as source inputs subject to owner policy approval.

modernized_recommendation.status: CONTROLLED BMC HTTPS CERTIFICATE REPLACEMENT TRANSACTION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a signed change record linking baseline certificate fingerprint, CSR fingerprint/public key, issued leaf and chain fingerprints, exact Redfish slot, replacement response, observed post-change server certificate and rollback result.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces unsafe placeholders and exposed defaults with an authorized CA/session workflow and adds deterministic target, trust, rollback and recovery controls.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful POST is not acceptance: the independently observed TLS leaf/chain/SAN and BMC service health must match the approved issuance, while inventory readback alone cannot prove client trust.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A syntactically valid but wrongly chained or mis-targeted certificate can immediately break all HTTPS automation; firmware may also restart the service or require a specific chain format.

project_override_considerations: The Project must decide whether the Apache setup is a required isolated test fixture or merely illustrative, map the mismatched placeholder artifact names, and approve an actual CA-capable chain. These are controlled execution inputs; the source's unambiguous CSR-sign-replace-verify objective is retained.
expected_evidence: Target/TLS identity, active fingerprint/chain, approvals, exact certificate URI, rollback and console-recovery proof
Protected CSR transaction and parsed public identity/key fields with no private key
Authorized issuance result and leaf/chain/SAN/validity/key-usage comparison
One protected replacement request/response tied to the exact slot
Independent client observation of installed fingerprint/chain, hostname validation and healthy Web/Redfish
Approved final or restored baseline state, audit/SEL/TLS evidence, no-secret exposure and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The intended CSR-sign-replace-verify lifecycle is consistent across Procedure and Criteria. Unsafe defaults, placeholder path/name mismatches and unclear Apache placement make the literal commands non-executable until owner mapping, but do not create competing test objectives.

blocked_analysis.analysis: An authorized CA workflow, supported certificate slot/schema, protected secrets and recovery artifact are normal project/security inputs; the case need not guess them and is not intrinsically unresolvable.

review_improvement: Preserves all cryptographic and replacement checkpoints while turning an unsafe placeholder recipe into a target-bound, secret-safe, reversible PKI transaction with independent TLS verification.
independent_technical_reasoning: Certificate replacement has a chain of identity invariants: the CSR public key and SAN must match the approved profile, the issued leaf must bind that same key, the replacement must target the intended slot, and an external client must observe the issued fingerprint and validate its chain. Breaking any link can yield a successful API response but an inaccessible or impersonated management endpoint, so rollback must exist before mutation.
